objectives: Map each phoneme to a known grapheme and write the complete word.
Read back the written word to verify the encoding.
concepts: Encoding moves from spoken word to phonemes to graphemes.
The new n grapheme can represent /n/ initially or finally in taught CVC words.
Read-back provides an immediate check between intended sounds and written form.

definitions.definition: Representing spoken sounds with written graphemes to spell a word.
Separating a spoken word into its individual sounds.
Connecting each phoneme to the written symbol that represents it.

workedExamples: map for nap → compare the first sound and replace m with n.
revisionPoints: Word → phonemes → graphemes → written word → read-back.

basic: Segment and spell nap and man.
conceptual: Identify which phoneme caused a spelling error.
application: Spell taught n-containing CVC words from dictation.
higherOrderThinking: Choose the correction step that matches the error.
mixedReview: Encode and read back CVC words using m/s/t/a/p/n.

weakTopicRevision: Practise one-sound contrasts before spelling the full CVC word again.

activities.name: Dictation map
steps: Map each sound to a grapheme.

activities.name: Read-back check
steps: Blend and compare with the original word.

outcomes: Learner segments taught CVC words with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner spells n-containing CVC words with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner correctly represents initial and final /n/ with n.
Learner uses read-back to detect and correct an encoding error.

questions.question: What should you do first when spelling a word you hear?
options: Say the word and segment its sounds

questions.question: After segmenting /m/ /a/ /n/, what should you do?
options: Map each sound to its grapheme and write it

questions.question: A learner writes “mat” for “man.” Which sound needs checking?
A learner writes “map” for “nap.” Which sound needs checking?
Why should the learner read the word after writing it?
options: To check that the written graphemes represent the intended sounds

questions.question: Which spelling has three graphemes and represents /n/ /a/ /p/?
Which spelling has initial /n/ and final /p/?
What is the main goal of this lesson?
options: Encode taught CVC words containing n accurately
